teaching_point: MACULE — flat, <1 cm colour change, not palpable (freckles/ephelides on sun-exposed arm). Close eyes and touch: no change in texture.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Freckles (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/ephelis

teaching_point: PATCH — flat area of colour change >1 cm. Symmetrical depigmented patches of vitiligo on the wrists (melanocyte loss).
dermnet_caption: Symmetrical wrist vitiligo - a common location
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Symmetrical wrist vitiligo - a common location (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/vitiligo

teaching_point: PATCH — café-au-lait 'macule' is >1 cm so technically a patch (DermNet/naming quirk); ≥6 CALMs → think neurofibromatosis type 1.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Café-au-lait macule (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cafe-au-lait-macule

teaching_point: PAPULE — raised, palpable, <1 cm. Flat-topped, shiny, polygonal violaceous papules of lichen planus on volar wrist (the '6 Ps').
dermnet_caption: Flat topped, shiny, polygonal papules of lichen planus on the volar wrist
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Flat topped, shiny, polygonal papules of lichen planus on the volar wrist (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/lichen-planus

teaching_point: PAPULE — dome-shaped pearly umbilicated papules of molluscum contagiosum (common in children; self-limiting).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Typical umbilicated papules (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/molluscum-contagiosum

teaching_point: PLAQUE — raised, flat-topped, >1 cm (broader than tall). Well-demarcated salmon-pink plaques with silvery scale = chronic plaque psoriasis.
dermnet_caption: Well demarcated plaques with silvery scale in chronic plaque psoriasis
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Well demarcated plaques with silvery scale in chronic plaque psoriasis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/psoriasis

teaching_point: NODULE — solid, palpable, >1 cm, often deeper (dermal/subcutaneous). Nodular BCC: pearly edge, telangiectasia, may ulcerate centrally — refer (NICE NG12 routine/2WW per context).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Nodular basal cell carcinoma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/basal-cell-carcinoma

teaching_point: NODULE — firm itchy nodules of nodular prurigo on the arms (driven by chronic scratching).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Nodular prurigo on the arms (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/nodular-prurigo

teaching_point: VESICLE — fluid-filled blister <1 cm (some texts 0.5 cm). Monomorphic vesicles / punched-out erosions of eczema herpeticum — same-day medical review.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Eczema herpeticum (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/eczema-herpeticum

teaching_point: VESICLE — 'dewdrop on a rose petal' vesicles of chickenpox (varicella), crops at different stages.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Chickenpox (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/chickenpox

teaching_point: BULLA — fluid-filled blister >1 cm. Tense (some haemorrhagic) bullae of bullous pemphigoid — subepidermal split so roof is thick and blisters stay intact.
dermnet_caption: Bullous pemphigoid (gallery image, no caption on page)
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Bullous pemphigoid (gallery image, no caption on page) (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/bullous-pemphigoid

teaching_point: BULLA — bullous pemphigoid blisters on the foot in skin of colour (older adults; check drug history e.g. gliptins).
dermnet_caption: Blisters of bullous pemphigoid on foot, skin of colour
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Blisters of bullous pemphigoid on foot, skin of colour (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/bullous-pemphigoid

teaching_point: PUSTULE — visible collection of pus (neutrophils) <1 cm. Follicular pustules in superficial bacterial folliculitis.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Superficial bacterial folliculitis (© Raimo Suhonen) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/folliculitis

teaching_point: PUSTULE — sterile pustules on the palm in palmoplantar pustulosis (pustule ≠ always infection; smokers).
dermnet_caption: Pustules on the palm due to PPP
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Pustules on the palm due to PPP (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/palmoplantar-pustulosis

teaching_point: WHEAL — transient, itchy, oedematous papule/plaque from dermal oedema; individual lesions resolve <24 h without marks (urticaria).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Urticaria (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/urticaria-an-overview

teaching_point: CYST — epithelium-lined sac containing fluid/semisolid material. Epidermoid cyst with central punctum (keratin-filled).
dermnet_caption: Epidermoid cyst with an obvious punctum
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Epidermoid cyst with an obvious punctum (© Raimo Suhonen) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/epidermoid-cyst

teaching_point: SCALE — visible flakes of excess stratum corneum (hyperkeratosis). Thick silvery scale on the elbow in psoriasis (extensor).
dermnet_caption: Thick silvery scale over the elbow
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Thick silvery scale over the elbow (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/psoriasis

teaching_point: SCALE — fine collarette scale on oval patches of pityriasis rosea along skin cleavage lines ('Christmas tree').
dermnet_caption: Oval scaly patches in pityriasis rosea on the trunk
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Oval scaly patches in pityriasis rosea on the trunk (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/pityriasis-rosea

teaching_point: CRUST — dried serum/blood/pus on the surface. Honey-coloured perioral crusts of non-bullous impetigo.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Perioral honey-coloured crusts in impetigo (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/impetigo

teaching_point: EROSION — partial loss of epidermis, heals without scar. Intact flaccid blister plus erosions in bullous impetigo (superficial split).
dermnet_caption: An intact blister and erosions in bullous impetigo
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — An intact blister and erosions in bullous impetigo (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/impetigo

teaching_point: EROSION — flaccid intraepidermal blisters of pemphigus rupture easily leaving erosions (contrast with tense BP bullae).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Pemphigus vulgaris (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/pemphigus-vulgaris

teaching_point: ULCER — full-thickness loss of epidermis + some dermis; heals with scar. Leg ulcer at gaiter area with surrounding venous pigmentation.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Leg ulcer (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/venous-insufficiency

teaching_point: FISSURE — linear crack through epidermis into dermis, painful. Glazed, cracked forefoot skin in juvenile plantar dermatosis.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Juvenile plantar dermatosis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/juvenile-plantar-dermatosis

teaching_point: FISSURE — macerated, cracked angles of the mouth in angular cheilitis (check candida/staph, dentures, iron/B12).
dermnet_caption: Bilateral angular cheilitis with grey maceration at the angles of the mouth
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Bilateral angular cheilitis with grey maceration at the angles of the mouth (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/angular-cheilitis

teaching_point: LICHENIFICATION — thickened skin with exaggerated skin markings from chronic rubbing/scratching (lichen simplex on the shin).
dermnet_caption: Localised lichen simplex on the lateral shin - a common area for this disorder
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Localised lichen simplex on the lateral shin - a common area for this disorder (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/lichen-simplex

teaching_point: ATROPHY — thinning of epidermis/dermis: shiny, translucent, wrinkled skin with visible vessels/purpura after prolonged potent topical steroid.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Skin thinning (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/topical-steroid

teaching_point: ATROPHY (dermal) — striae in a flexure from potent topical steroid: counselling point on potency, site and duration.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Stretch marks (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/topical-steroid

teaching_point: EXCORIATION — linear/punctate erosions caused by scratching; marker of itch (here excoriated prurigo papules).
dermnet_caption: Excoriated papules on the arms in nodular prurigo
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Excoriated papules on the arms in nodular prurigo (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/nodular-prurigo

teaching_point: SCAR — fibrous tissue replacing damaged dermis. Hypertrophic scar stays within the wound boundary.
dermnet_caption: A hypertrophic scar on the upper back - the thickening does not extend beyond the confines of the injury
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A hypertrophic scar on the upper back - the thickening does not extend beyond the confines of the injury (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/keloid-and-hypertrophic-scar

teaching_point: SCAR — keloid extends beyond original wound (earlobe after piercing); more common in skin types V–VI.
dermnet_caption: A large 'dumbbell' keloid on the earlobe
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A large 'dumbbell' keloid on the earlobe (© Dr Richard Ashton) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/keloid-and-hypertrophic-scar

teaching_point: ANNULAR — ring-shaped with clearer centre. Granuloma annulare: smooth (no scale) ring on dorsal hand vs scaly-edged tinea.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Granuloma annulare (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/granuloma-annulare

teaching_point: TARGET (iris) — three-zone lesions on hands in erythema multiforme (acral distribution).
dermnet_caption: Cutaneous adverse reaction to anticonvulsant, erythema multiforme target lesions
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Cutaneous adverse reaction to anticonvulsant, erythema multiforme target lesions (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/erythema-multiforme

teaching_point: LINEAR — papules lined up along a scratch (Koebner phenomenon) in lichen planus; also psoriasis, vitiligo, warts.
dermnet_caption: Papular lichen planus with a linear Koebner lesion due to a scratch
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Papular lichen planus with a linear Koebner lesion due to a scratch (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/lichen-planus

teaching_point: DERMATOMAL — unilateral band of grouped vesicles on erythema not crossing the midline (herpes zoster).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Herpes zoster (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/herpes-zoster

teaching_point: FLEXURAL — well-demarcated salmon-pink erythema in a skin fold with little scale (flexural/inverse psoriasis).
dermnet_caption: Well demarcated salmon pink erythema which extends to the apex of the skin fold due to flexural psoriasis
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Well demarcated salmon pink erythema which extends to the apex of the skin fold due to flexural psoriasis (© Dr Ph Abimelec - dermatologue) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/psoriasis

teaching_point: EXTENSOR — dry atopic dermatitis on extensor elbow (extensor pattern typical in infants; psoriasis also favours extensors).
dermnet_caption: Dry atopic dermatitis in an extensor pattern
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Dry atopic dermatitis in an extensor pattern (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/atopic-dermatitis

teaching_point: Layers: epidermis → basement membrane → dermis → subcutis. Use to explain level of split (vesicle/bulla), wheal (dermal oedema), nodule (deep dermis).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Skin structure (Open access image) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/the-structure-of-normal-skin

teaching_point: Fitzpatrick I — always burns, never tans; freckles, red hair: highest UV skin-cancer risk; strict photoprotection.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Phototype I (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/skin-phototype

teaching_point: Fitzpatrick IV — burns minimally, tans easily; higher PIH risk; more UV needed for vitamin D synthesis.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Phototype IV (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/skin-phototype

teaching_point: Fitzpatrick VI — deeply pigmented, never burns; erythema harder to see; marked PIH/keloid tendency; vitamin D deficiency risk in UK.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Phototype VI (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/skin-phototype

teaching_point: Post-inflammatory pigment change in skin of colour — resolving psoriasis leaves hypopigmented marks; counsel that colour change is common in darker phototypes.
dermnet_caption: Post-inflammatory hypopigmentation as guttate psoriasis is resolving
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Post-inflammatory hypopigmentation as guttate psoriasis is resolving (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/plaque-psoriasis

teaching_point: Dermoscopy of solar lentigo — light-brown homogeneous pigment, moth-eaten border (contrast with lentigo maligna).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Dermoscopy of a solar lentigo (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/solar-lentigo

teaching_point: Dermoscopy of molluscum — central polylobular white structures with crown vessels; dermoscopy is more than a 'torch'.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Molluscum contagiosum (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/molluscum-contagiosum

teaching_point: Quiz case match — flexural atopic dermatitis in a child (antecubital fossa); itch disturbs sleep.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Flexural atopic dermatitis in childhood (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/atopic-dermatitis

teaching_point: Chronic flexural AD: thickening, accentuated skin creases, hyperpigmentation = LICHENIFICATION.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Chronic flexural atopic dermatitis (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/atopic-dermatitis

teaching_point: Lichenification plus excoriations — both are secondary changes of the itch–scratch cycle (SCORAD scores both).
dermnet_caption: Excoriated lichenified atopic dermatitis on the lower back in an adult
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Excoriated lichenified atopic dermatitis on the lower back in an adult (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/atopic-dermatitis

teaching_point: Lichenification in skin of colour — accentuated markings, scale and hyperpigmentation (not just redness).
dermnet_caption: Lichen simplex on the ankles - accentuated skin markings, scale and pigmentation in skin of colour
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Lichen simplex on the ankles - accentuated skin markings, scale and pigmentation in skin of colour (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/lichen-simplex

teaching_point: Eczema herpeticum: primary lesions are VESICLES (monomorphic, umbilicated); here they have evolved into punched-out erosions and crusts, which are SECONDARY.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Eczema herpeticum (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/eczema-herpeticum
